body.input: Which health tech companies expanded to Denmark in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, here are health tech companies that have expanded to or within Denmark in 2026:

## Notable Expansions & Market Entries

- **Wellster HealthTech** (Germany-based) — Europe's leading Direct-to-Patient HealthTech platform is actively expanding into the Nordics in 2026, with Denmark as a key target market. The company is hiring an International Growth Manager for the Nordics and plans to launch its **GoLighter** GLP-1 weight-management brand in Sweden, Denmark, and Finland. Wellster secured a €10 million debt facility from Claret Capital Partners specifically to fund this international expansion.

- **Cisco** — The US tech company has deepened its engagement with Danish regional governments and the Danish healthcare sector, working on public-private partnership projects focused on patient-centric remote care and network infrastructure for health IT.

## Denmark's Growing HealthTech Ecosystem (2026)

Denmark's health tech sector has grown significantly, with **734 HealthTech companies** now operating in the country (205 funded, 72 at Series A or higher). Notable 2026 funding rounds for Denmark-based health tech companies include:

- **Dawn Health** — Raised a Series C round in February 2026 (investors include Cipio Partners)
- **Hi Rasmus** — Raised a Series C round in September 2026 (investor: Updata)
- **Aisel Health** — Raised a €1.7M pre-seed/seed round in August 2026 (led by Caesar Ventures) for its AI-powered psychiatry platform; the company is also expanding from Denmark into the UK
- **Kvantify** — Raised a Seed round in March 2026

The HealthTech SaaS sector alone in Denmark has seen **$58.1 million** in total funding in 2026 to date.

It's worth noting that specific announcements of international health tech companies opening new offices or formally entering Denmark in 2026 are limited in available reporting. Denmark's strength as a health IT leader — spending only 10.5% of GDP on healthcare compared to the US's 17.9% — continues to attract interest from global players, but many expansions may not yet be publicly documented.

# Denmark-based HealthTech Startup Aisel Health Raises €1.7M Pre-Seed to Expand AI Psychiatry Platform Into the UK

The Caesar Ventures-led round will support the development of Aisel Health’s AI-powered clinical operating system, engineering expansion and entry into the UK psychiatric healthcare market.

3 days ago

Arab Founders

Aisel Health, a Denmark-based HealthTech startup developing an artificial intelligence-powered clinical operating system for psychiatry, has raised €1.7 million in a Pre-Seed funding round led by Caesar Ventures.

The investment attracted participation from Nordic Web Ventures, LifeX and Angel Invest, alongside existing investors Rockstart and EIFO. [...] The company’s approach combines AI-assisted information processing with the clinical expertise required for psychiatric assessment and treatment.

## Expanding Clinical Research and Partnerships in Denmark

Aisel Health is already working with private psychiatric clinics in Denmark as it develops and evaluates its technology.

These collaborations provide opportunities to understand clinical workflows and refine the platform based on the needs of healthcare professionals.

The startup is also conducting research with partners including the University of Southern Denmark.

The research activities are intended to support the development of technology suited to the complexities of psychiatric care. [...] Its planned expansion will allow the company to introduce its technology to a larger international market and evaluate demand beyond Denmark.

The UK entry will also provide opportunities to develop relationships with additional healthcare organizations and gather feedback from different clinical environments.

Aisel Health intends to use the Pre-Seed investment to support this expansion while continuing to develop its core platform.

The company is also preparing for a future Seed funding round as it works to strengthen its commercial position.

Details regarding the timing and target size of the planned Seed round have not been disclosed.
